institutionName: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The most crucial aspects for me were: 
- That the destination was international and I could easily communicate in English
- A total different and new culture to my home country
- That the university offered had a good reputation and interesting courses for me

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, they sent a lot of emails for the exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a meeting with all exchange students to explain what we need to know and we were also assigned a coordinator in each hall.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were double rooms or rooms shared by four, but I do not remember if you could chose a double room.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of food options, even international food (McDonlad's, Subway, italian restaurant, kebabs), not just asian.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The campus is huge, so it is a little bit overwhelming at first, but appart from that, you have everything you need there(supermarket, gym, library, swimming pool, access to the beach, etc).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The room was nice, but I would prefer to live by my own.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before arriving we needed to create our email and Canvas account. Once at the campus, we needed to register at the hall were we lived and pick up our stundent ID, which was used to enter the residential halls, library, gym, etc., all the facilities in the university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could either contact exchange coordinators or you assigned hall coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was rejected from the courses at Mater's level, as we were only allowed to take undergraduated courses. For those, for exchange students they ask for some proof that you are qualified (you have the basic knowledge) to take the course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Some teachers need proof that you are legitimate to take that course, so be prepared to offer some proof.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Exchange students were not allowed to take MA courses. However, the BA courses were already quite intensive. Specially in my case, where I chose Computer Science courses, the level of programming was above mine (even being a master's student). The lectures are intensive and we also had a lot of assignments (labs) and Programming assignments to do.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is not very different, as the lectures are completely theoretical and then we also had TA session in case we needed help with the assignments. The only difference is that in some courses we also had lab sessions that were mandatory to attend.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
COMP 2012	OOP and Data Structures		 
COMP 3021	Java Programming	
COMP 3211	Fundamentals of A. I.
COMP 4461	Human-Computer Interaction

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If the student is interested in learn a programming language in more depth, I recommend COMP 2012 and COMP 3021, as they only focused on C++ and Java programming (respectively) in a very intensive way.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to go to the hospital, which is covered, but in case they need to open any medical material or you need drugs, you have to pay for that. If you have a travel insurance, they will cover that.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was much less expensive than I excepted (except coffee).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Although I did not participate in any, there were a lot of options, all of them very interesting.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of sport clubs (football, badmintong, sailing, martial arts, etc), cultural clubs (gaming, music, environemnt, etc).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I do not know, I did not take any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travelling from Hong Kong was very easy, so if you have time, visit other countries. In HK there are a lot of things to do as well. The university also prepares day tours and hiking the first days.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: For me was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are very shy, so just be nice and see if they want to interact.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Cars do not stop at the crosswalks for pedestrians, and burping and farting in public is normal.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The generosity and helpfulness of the people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Ask for help to reach the residential hall. 
2. Go everywhere with at least 10 minutes of anticipation (the campus is huge). 
3. Download the Octopus for tourists app to pay at the canteens and the bus.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting all the people I have met and travelling.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Some of the courses were harder than I though.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
